ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Back Concord Music Group's AI Suit Against Anthropic
ip_top_stories.summary: Major publishers and media groups have filed support for Concord Music Group's copyright lawsuit against Anthropic, signalling a broadening coalition of content industries opposing AI training practices. The backing underscores growing industry coordination in AI copyright litigation. The story is covered by Publishers Weekly, a primary trade source.

ip_top_stories.title: Penguin to Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Version of German Children's Book
ip_top_stories.summary: German children's book publisher Penguin is suing OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT reproduced a German children's book in a way that infringes copyright. The case adds to a growing body of European publisher litigation against AI companies over training data and output reproduction.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic's Amodei Seeks Copyright Deal That 'Works for Everyone'
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has publicly called for a copyright framework that balances the interests of AI developers and content creators, amid ongoing litigation and regulatory scrutiny in Australia and elsewhere. His comments come as Anthropic faces multiple copyright disputes globally.

ip_top_stories.title: UK Government Maintains Status Quo on AI and Copyright, Playing the Long Game on Potential Reform
ip_top_stories.summary: The UK government has declined to make immediate legislative changes to copyright law in relation to AI, opting instead to monitor developments and gather further evidence before committing to reform. The decision leaves creators and AI companies in continued uncertainty over training data rights.

ip_top_stories.title: French Private Members' Bill Aims to Protect Creatives' Copyright from AI Usage
ip_top_stories.summary: A private members' bill introduced in the French legislature seeks to give creators stronger rights to control and be compensated for the use of their work in AI training. The proposal reflects broader European legislative momentum to address AI and copyright tensions.

ip_further_links.title: What AI Asks of Open Access
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the open access movement intersects with AI training data demands, raising questions about whether open licences intended for human readers are appropriate for large-scale machine ingestion.

ip_further_links.title: Cloudflare Legal Chief on AI Bots and Publisher Revenue Loss
ip_further_links.summary: Cloudflare's chief legal officer discusses how AI crawlers are affecting publisher revenues, the challenge of overblocking, and the company's approach to managing AI bot traffic.

ip_further_links.title: Q&A: The UK's Copyright Report – A Gift to Creators, A Problem for AI
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the UK's recent copyright report, exploring its implications for creators and the challenges it poses for AI developers seeking to use copyrighted content for training.

ip_further_links.title: How African Creators Are Currently Being Exploited in the AI Boom
ip_further_links.summary: An examination of how African creators' works are being used to train AI systems with little compensation or consent, highlighting a global equity gap in AI copyright protections.

ip_further_links.title: Is Copyright Law the Wrong Weapon Against AI?
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece questions whether copyright litigation is the most effective mechanism for regulating AI training data use, suggesting alternative legal or regulatory approaches may be needed.

ip_further_links.title: How India Is Trying to Navigate AI Copyright's Three-Body Problem
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of India's complex challenge in balancing the interests of AI developers, content creators, and the public as it develops its approach to AI copyright regulation.

ip_further_links.title: Media Bosses: 'Australia Shouldn't Be Held to Ransom' by AI Giants
ip_further_links.summary: Australian media executives are pushing back against AI companies' use of their content without compensation, calling for stronger regulatory action and licensing frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Harlequin to Co-Produce AI-Generated 'Microdramas'
ip_further_links.summary: Publisher Harlequin has announced plans to co-produce a slate of AI-generated short-form video content, raising questions about AI's role in creative publishing and authorship.

ip_further_links.title: Beyond Copyright: Why Asia Pacific Governments Must Govern AI Training Data as Public Infrastructure
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary argues that Asia Pacific governments should treat AI training data governance as a matter of public infrastructure policy rather than relying solely on copyright frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: AI Content Ownership Remains Legally Undefined as Studios and Creators Brace for Court Battles
ip_further_links.summary: Legal uncertainty over who owns AI-generated content persists as the entertainment industry and individual creators prepare for a wave of litigation to clarify rights.
